item.title: Gemini 3.1 Pro
item.description: Gemini 3.1 Pro is Google’s flagship coding and reasoning model — Gemini 3.5 Pro hasn’t shipped yet, so 3.1 Pro remains the top tier of the Gemini line for complex, multi-step work.

item.title: Google Drive
item.description:
The Google Drive server lets an agent search your Drive and read the contents of documents and spreadsheets, using OAuth scoped to your account.

Why it matters

A lot of real work context — specs, meeting notes, planning docs — lives in Docs and Sheets, not in a codebase. This connector lets an agent reference that material directly instead of you manually copying content into a prompt.

item.title: Gemini CLI
item.description: Gemini CLI is Google’s open-source command-line agent built on Gemini models: it works directly against a local repository from the terminal, answering questions about the code, making edits, and running commands as part of a multi-step task.

item.title: Google Antigravity
item.description: Antigravity reframes the IDE around managing agents rather than writing code directly: a standalone desktop app lets you run several Gemini-powered coding agents in parallel, schedule automated tasks, and give agents built-in browser automation to test and verify their own work.

item.title: Firebase Studio
item.description:
Firebase Studio is Google’s browser-based development environment, evolved from Project IDX, that combines a full cloud IDE with Gemini-powered app generation, previews, and one-click deployment through Firebase.

Why it stands out

  • Runs entirely in the browser, spinning up a cloud workspace with no local setup required.
  • Gemini-driven app scaffolding, able to generate a working full-stack app from a prompt and iterate on it inside the same workspace.
  • Direct path to deployment, since workspaces connect straight into Firebase App Hosting and other Google Cloud services.

Good for

Developers building on Firebase or Google Cloud who want AI-assisted scaffolding and deployment without leaving the browser.

item.title: Google Antigravity Skills System
item.description:
Google Antigravity’s skills system supports the same SKILL.md format as Claude Code and Codex, with both global (~/.gemini/config/skills/) and per-project (.agents/skills/) scopes.

Why a skill for this

Supporting the shared SKILL.md format means skills built for Antigravity aren’t locked to Google’s tooling — the same skill folder is portable to other compatible agents.

item.title: Gemini CLI Skills System
item.description:
Gemini CLI natively supports the Agent Skills (SKILL.md) open standard, letting it load the same skill format used by Claude Code, Codex, and other compatible agents.

Why a skill for this

A shared skills format means a skill only has to be written once to work across Gemini CLI and other compatible agents, rather than maintaining separate versions per tool.
